<!--- boilerplate: notify --->

Looking more at this block of code and the `syspatch(8)` options, I think when `apply` is false `check_flag` should be `['-c']` and when `apply` is true `check_flag` should be `[]`. I'll flip those around.

I'll also try to understand `run_flag` better, and ensure it's set properly.

> I'll flip those around.

I think I misunderstood what `check_flag` and `run_flag` are for, in this Ansible module. Here's where they're used:

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/63b94fca7e96a0fe9fcb92d3af3097e3a309f5ab/lib/ansible/modules/system/syspatch.py#L118-L119

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/63b94fca7e96a0fe9fcb92d3af3097e3a309f5ab/lib/ansible/modules/system/syspatch.py#L133-L134

Should `check_flag` should always be `-c` and `run_flag` be empty, `-R`, or `-r` based on the parameters provided? What should `module.run_command(cmd + check_flag)` accomplish when the user asks to `revert` `all`? or `revert` `one`?

[The syspatch module doc](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/modules/syspatch_module.html#syspatch-module) describes four modes of operation with two parameters. `apply` is boolean, `revert` can be "all" or "one", and the two parameters are mutually exclusive. Here are the [`syspatch(8)` syntax](https://man.openbsd.org/syspatch) for each:

apply | revert | syntax
-|-|-
True | _unset_ | `syspatch`
False | _unset_ | `syspatch -c`
_unset_ | all | `syspatch -R`
_unset_ | one | `syspatch -r`

`syspatch(8)` has four options (plus a default mode), so we could, for example, simplify the module to use one parameter like `option` which the user can set to "install-all", "check", "list", "revert-one", or "revert-all". If we want to maintain backward compatibility:

apply | revert | option | syntax
-|-|-|-
True | _unset_ | _unset_ | `syspatch`
False | _unset_ | _unset_ | `syspatch -c`
_unset_ | all | _unset_ | `syspatch -R`
_unset_ | one | _unset_ | `syspatch -r`
_unset_ | _unset_ | install-all | `syspatch`
_unset_ | _unset_ | check | `syspatch -c`
_unset_ | _unset_ | list | `syspatch -l`
_unset_ | _unset_ | revert-all | `syspatch -R`
_unset_ | _unset_ | revert-one | `syspatch -r`

Anyway, for now I'll close this PR, find another way to run `syspatch`, and look forward to the changes proposed in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/63738 and https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/57259.
